title: Fibrewise regular equations cut a flat slice of a stack presentation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, $q:U\to\mathcal X$ a flat locally finitely presented morphism from a scheme, and $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ a map from a field. Put $F=U\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $p:F\to U$ be the projection. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ with $r\geq0$, and suppose there is an etale map $V\to F$ from a scheme and a point $v\in V$ where the pullbacks of the $f_i$ form an $\mathcal O_{V,v}$-regular sequence. Let $u$ be the image of $v$ in $U$. There is an open neighbourhood $U_1$ of $u$ such that the closed subscheme $Z=V(f_1|_{U_1},\ldots,f_r|_{U_1})\subset U_1$ is flat and locally of finite presentation over $\mathcal X$. Regular sequence, closed subscheme, open subscheme, flatness and local finite presentation use [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; etale uses [def-weil-etale-morphism]. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre product and representability by algebraic spaces use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts.

source.place: Tag 06MD (lemma-slice), scheme-source specialization; the etale-chart formulation of the regular-sequence hypothesis is the strict-local-ring formulation there, since these local maps are faithfully flat.

proof.text: Write $z$ for the image of $v$ in $F$. Choose a geometric point $\bar v$ centered at $v$, and put $\bar z=e\bar v$ for the given etale map $e:V\to F$. By [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness], $\mathcal O_{F,\bar z}\cong\mathcal O_{V,v}^{\mathrm{sh}}$, compatibly with germs of all the $f_i$. The map from $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ to this strict henselization is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. Hence [lem-sfb-regular-sequence-faithfully-flat-ascent] carries the given regular sequence to $\mathcal O_{F,\bar z}$.

source.place: Tags 04KF (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization), and algebra.tex Tag 00LM (lemma-flat-increases-depth); initial chart-to-strict-local comparison in Tag 06MD.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $W\to\mathcal X$, which exists by the algebraic-stack hypothesis. The field-extension lifting formulation of surjectivity in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to the atlas and $a$, supplies a field extension $k'/k$ and $w:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to W$ together with a 2-isomorphism from its composite to $a|_{k'}$. Set $T=U\times_{\mathcal X}W$. These fibre products are algebraic spaces: the diagonal of $\mathcal X$ is representable, so the product of the two scheme sources over $\mathcal X$ is its base change. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $T\to W$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and $\pi:T\to U$ is smooth. The 2-isomorphism gives $F':=T\times_W\operatorname{Spec}k'\cong F\times_k k'$, compatibly with maps to $U$: on an $S$-scheme $B$, an object on the left specifies $b:B\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$, $x:B\to U$, and $\alpha:q(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}w(b)$ in $\mathcal X(B)$. Compose $\alpha$ with the chosen $w\cong a|_{k'}$ to get the object on the right; composing with its inverse reverses this operation. Both operations preserve arrows and pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 06MD (lemma-slice), first paragraph and the second cartesian diagram.

proof.text: The projection $F\times_k k'\to F$ is flat and surjective, as can be checked on etale affine charts: an affine $k$-chart with ring $D$ becomes $D\otimes_k k'$, and [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] makes this ring map faithfully flat. Its map on spectra is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]; the jointly surjective etale charts of [def-trf-algebraic-space] then cover every point of $F$. Choose $z'\in|F'|$ over $z$, and compatible geometric points $\bar z',\bar z$ after a common algebraically closed extension. For this extension the separable algebraic closure of each residue field inside the old algebraically closed field is already its separable algebraic closure inside the new one: any element algebraic over the residue field is algebraic over the old algebraically closed field and hence lies in it. On an etale scheme chart, each pointed etale neighbourhood has finite separable residue extension at its marked point. Its residue embeddings into the larger algebraically closed field therefore already land in the old separable closure, and their compatibility is unchanged. Thus the indexing triples and their ring maps, hence the colimits defining the old strict local ring, agree. This is the construction of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. By [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness] the resulting homomorphism $\mathcal O_{F,\bar z}\to\mathcal O_{F',\bar z'}$ is flat and local; it is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-sequence-faithfully-flat-ascent] to the sequence from step 1. Thus the pulled-back $f_i$ are regular in $\mathcal O_{F',\bar z'}$.

source.place: Tag 06MD (lemma-slice), middle paragraph; Tag 04NG (spaces-morphisms lemma-flat-at-point-etale-local-rings), Tag 00LM (algebra lemma-flat-increases-depth).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-fibre-regular-slice-flat] to $T\to W$, the field point $w$, the pulled-back sections, and $\bar z'$. All its hypotheses hold: flatness and local finite presentation are from step 2, its fibre is $F'$ there, and its regularity hypothesis is step 3. It gives an open subspace $T'\subset T$ containing the image $t'$ of $z'$ such that $H=T'\cap V(f_1|_T,\ldots,f_r|_T)$ is flat and locally of finite presentation over $W$.

The morphism $\pi|_{T'}:T'\to U$ is smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. By [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open] its image $U_1$ is open, and $u\in U_1$ because $t'\in T'$ maps to $u$. Factor $T'\to U$ through this open image. The factor $T'\to U_1$ is the base change of $T'\to U$ along $U_1\hookrightarrow U$: a map to $T'$ already maps into $U_1$, so $T'\times_U U_1\cong T'$. Thus it is smooth by the cited base-change clause, and surjective on points by the definition of $U_1$ as the image. It is also surjective in the field-extension lifting convention of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], which is that of the source-descent input: given $y:\operatorname{Spec}K\to U_1$ at a point $u_1$, choose a point of $T'$ over $u_1$ and, on an etale scheme chart of $T'$, a field point $\operatorname{Spec}K_1\to T'$ at it. Both $K$ and $K_1$ are extensions of $\kappa(u_1)$, so $K\otimes_{\kappa(u_1)}K_1\neq0$; a residue field $L$ at one of its maximal ideals contains both, and $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K_1\to T'$ lifts $y|_L$. Put $Z=V(f_1|_{U_1},\ldots,f_r|_{U_1})$. There is a canonical identification $H\cong T'\times_{U_1}Z$: on affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U_1$, the pullback of $Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A A/(f_1,\ldots,f_r))=\operatorname{Spec}(B/(f_1B,\ldots,f_rB))$. These quotient identifications commute with chart restrictions, so identify the closed subspaces. Therefore $H\to Z$ is smooth and surjective by the base-change clauses of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus].

source.place: Tag 06MD (lemma-slice), last paragraph; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 042S (lemma-fppf-open). Surjectivity conventions: stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XI (lemma-characterize-surjective), as stated in the cited stack calculus.

proof.text: By step 4, $H\to W$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The atlas $W\to\mathcal X$ has those properties since it is smooth. The composition $H\to\mathcal X$ is consequently flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The maps $H\to Z$ and $Z\to\mathcal X$ are representable by algebraic spaces: for the former both objects are algebraic spaces, and for the latter both scheme sources over $\mathcal X$ have algebraic-space fibre product by the representable-diagonal argument of step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-cover-flat-lfp-descent] to $H\to Z\to\mathcal X$, using the smooth surjectivity established in step 5 in the field-extension lifting convention of that descent statement. It follows that $Z\to\mathcal X$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, as required. This also covers $r=0$: the zero ideal gives the whole source and all uses of regularity concern the empty list in a nonzero local ring.
